source.title: Abstraction Mechanisms Predict Generalization in Deep Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that networks memorize a Gaussian-noise dataset with random labels, a conceptual test of fitting unstructured inputs. It does not report the other fitting behaviors in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorizing random datasets; those citations are not treated as results. Its own Gaussian-noise result is retained. Label-corruption experiments are described as evaluations of generalization metrics, without reported training-fit outcomes.
record.test_reason: Section 4.3 reports the study's own networks memorizing randomly labeled Gaussian inputs, directly bearing on random-label fitting and fitting unstructured inputs using the original training-and-memorization approach.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that CNA predicts task performance and that CNA-Margin predicts generalization gaps across varied datasets and architectures, outperforming compared metrics especially under dataset corruption; they encourage further investigation of abstraction mechanisms and generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains networks on randomly labeled Gaussian-noise inputs and reports memorization, but its experiments primarily evaluate a generalization metric rather than reproduce the original random-labeling experiment on training images.

fits_no_version.finding: CNA-Margin correlates with generalization gaps comparatively robustly when Gaussian data or corrupted labels are included.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CNA-Margin predicts generalization gaps under dataset corruption better than the compared metrics.

record.problems: The Gaussian-noise memorization statement gives no training-error value, test error, architecture list for that dataset, or training details. Label-corruption results are reported as metric comparisons rather than direct training-fit measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were reported. The label-corruption experiments in Section 4.3 and Figure 7B report generalization-metric comparisons, not the training-fit outcomes required for V4.

untested.parts: Chance test error, unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters, and use of stochastic gradient methods are not established for the Gaussian experiment.
Relative training time and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Shuffled-pixel and independently permuted-pixel inputs; numerical confirmation of zero training error.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions. The 10%–50% label-corruption experiments report metric correlations rather than these outcomes.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on memorization and generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before noisy labels and comparisons of real-label versus random-label learning dynamics.

record.verdict_notes: Memorization is explicitly reported, but exact zero training error is not quantified. Unreported protocol details do not constitute contrary results. The supplied text references a supplement whose training details are not included.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling of training images, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and generalization on true labels are not tested in the reported results.
Training-time comparison and convergence as corruption increases are not reported.
Gaussian-noise inputs with random labels are reported as memorized; shuffled-pixel and independently permuted-pixel inputs are not tested.
The paper evaluates metrics on datasets with 10% to 50% shuffled labels but does not report training fit or test-error progression across corruption levels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization are not tested.
The paper does not measure learning order or compare how real and random labels are learned.
